title.narrative: Protection, NFI and Emergency Shelter Response targeting Conflict affected communities in Kismayo, Dhobley, Gagodob, Jariban and South Mudug.

description.narrative: Puntland, Galmudug as well as Jubaland states have experienced an escalation of displacements resulting from both inter-clan conflicts and military action respectively. In Mudug, power struggles between various clans, each vying for control and influence over different regions, have fueled the violence which has resulted to the displacement of more than 50,000 individuals. Incidents are typically related to disputes over grazing fields and unresolved clan revenge disputes. The inter-clan dispute between the sub-clans is related to contested land ownership and the construction of water dams. The violent disputes started in May and escalated through July, with more than ten clashes recorded around Galdogob and Gaalkacyo towns. At least 70 people were reportedly killed and hundreds more injured. Similar violence was also reported in Abudwak, Galmudug - this time of retaliatory nature following the killing of a prominent clan elder. In Lower Juba the humanitarian situation has significantly deteriorated following the Black Lion operation in late 2023, leading to the government's withdrawal from strategic towns. Jubaland security forces and Danab special forces launched an operation targeting Alshabab group’s stronghold positions in the Lower and Middle Juba regions in Jubaland state. By July, security forces had taken control of five villages south of Afmadow after clashes with al-Shabaab. Clashes between al-Shabaab and security forces spread in villages in the Kismayo district, resulting in dozens of reported fatalities. According to PSMN, a total of 159,000 individuals have been displaced outside their districts of habitation while hundred thousand others are stranded within the districts where conflict is ongoing. These displaced communities have left their homes, and are living rough in makeshift structures within informal settlements and with minimal or no access to any humanitarian assistance. Their protection situation is highly jeopardized - particularly women, girls, children and persons with specific needs, including the elderly and the disabled. The affected populations mainly lacks access to critical protection services, emergency shelter and NFIs, food and clean water. The humanitarian situation in the three most affected states - Puntland, Galmudug and Jubaland- continues to be critical since these locations were already struggling to recover from a series of devastating events, including the 2020-2023 droughts and the 2023 El Niño-induced floods, which caused widespread displacement, destruction of infrastructure, and disruption of essential services.As a response, UNHCR will implement (1) an integrated protection response targeting 20,000 people in Kismayo, Dhobley, Gagodob, Jariban and South Mudug through the establishment and management of Protection Desks, provision of Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), Community-Based Protection which will also encompass Child protection, GBV prevention and response through assessments for identification of vulnerable cases and referrals; (2) New arrival protection monitoring, counselling and identification of protection and specific needs with ensuing emergency protection response as well as integrated response with protective shelter and core relief targeting 50,400 individuals for stronger protection outcomes; and (3) Enhancing protection mainstreaming across other sectoral interventions - such as food, to enable an inclusive, safe and non-discriminatory response.
